statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail returns to the low band after a completed two-way session, while Stress stays elevated on multi-decade-high long-end yields and a 17% month-to-date crude advance.
recommendation: Thursday's session opened with a gap lower, based at 30,204.16, fully retraced and closed marginally above its prior close, so mean reversion functioned in both directions across the whole range. Volatility decayed into the close with VIX back to 15.60 from a 16.57 high. Stress remains elevated because the 10-year is near its highest since 2007, the 30-year near a 2004 high, and crude is up more than 3% on an unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff. The narrow danger window covers Friday's 12:30Z Durable Goods release and the 13:30Z US cash open. Tail remains below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100 fully retraces its gap and closes flat at 30,478.86; Tail returns to the low band with Stress elevated on record long-end yields
body: NDX closed at 30,478.86, up 8.56 points or 0.03%, against a 30,470.29 prior close. The session opened at 30,225.19, roughly 0.8% below the prior close, based at 30,204.16, then retraced the entire gap to a 30,529.35 high before settling just above the prior close. That 325-point range, about 1.07%, was traded in both directions with completed retracements and the close printed in the upper half of it. This is the central reason Tail returns to the low band: the day's structure is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the contract defines as tail risk. VIX closed at 15.60, up 2.76% on the day but well below its 16.57 session high and off a 15.34 low, so the volatility impulse decayed rather than extended. The stress backdrop nonetheless remains genuinely difficult. The Treasury sold roughly $44bn of 7-year notes at a 5.085% high yield, the highest since April 1993, tailing a 5.078% market yield with bid-to-cover at 2.42 against 2.50 last month and indirect bidders down to 57.2% from about 61%. The 10-year traded near 5.10-5.14%, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year near 5.43%, its highest since 2004, while the H.15 release for 23 September carried the 2-year at 4.85%, the 10-year at 5.11% and the 30-year at 5.40%. The curve is steepening on term premium rather than policy repricing. WTI is near $95.29, up 3.39%, and Brent near $107.52, up 4.31%, after a $108.23 Brent session high driven by a Houthi missile barrage fired at Saudi Arabia; Brent is up more than 17% in September. Prices then pulled back on a Reuters report that US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased deal under which Iran would permit navigation through the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for Washington ending its naval blockade. A senior Iranian official framed that as the most realistic path, while Iran has also said it will not allow freedom of navigation while sanctions and the blockade remain. That is a genuinely two-sided catalyst and it is unresolved, which is why it informs Stress and the danger-window placement rather than the current Tail score. Today's US data added to the yield pressure: initial claims printed 197K against a 201K consensus and continuing claims 1,719K, new home sales beat at 0.684M, and good data backfired by lifting yields. Oracle fell sharply after Bloomberg reported a force majeure notice on its New Mexico data centre project, which weighs on AI-infrastructure sentiment without having produced index-level one-way structure. Per the risk contract, a weak auction, a hawkish yield impulse, an energy shock and high-importance headlines raise Stress and inform Confidence; they do not establish Tail on their own. Tail would require observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed retracements and a hold near session extremes. A full gap retrace and a flat close are evidence against that path. Shared Finviz context was about 170 minutes old and partial at the cutoff, with its calendar and futures sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale supporting evidence only and every current level was taken from primary sources.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 published hours stayed inside a watch-band regime with a single orange print. Tail ran 20-23 through Wednesday's late US session, eased to 17-19 across the Asian overnight as conditions normalised, then rebuilt through a trend-down European morning to a 25 peak at 09:00Z, the only BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES slot in the window. Across the US session it oscillated between 19 and 24 without establishing a one-way path, printing 20 at 16:00Z, 19 at 17:00Z, 21 at 18:00Z and 20 at 19:00Z. Stress stepped up from the high 40s overnight to the mid-to-high 50s as the long-end selloff deepened, and Confidence held in a tight 85-88 band throughout. Dominant mode was mixed for most of the window, normal across the quiet overnight, and trend-down during the bond-driven European morning.
outlookSummary: The base case is continued two-way trade around Thursday's 30,204-30,529 range. Conditional Tail eases to 18-19 across the US evening and Asian overnight, where the published lookback repeatedly mean-reverted, with a one-point nudge for the 22:00Z CME electronic reopen. It rebuilds to 20-22 into the European open and through the European morning, which carried this window's highest published Tail, then peaks at 24 in the 13:00Z slot where the 12:30Z Durable Goods release and the 13:30Z US cash open stack together. That slot and the preceding one define the narrow danger window. Conditional Tail then decays to 21-23 through the US afternoon as event dispersion resolves, with a one-point lift into the Friday power hour for weekend-risk reduction around the unresolved Hormuz negotiation. No slot reaches the blocking threshold, because that would require observed shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or extreme-holding that cannot be established from this cutoff. Confidence steps down from 88 to 80 across the forecast as distance from the verified evidence base grows.
